item.title: Akiyoshidai Plateau: Japan's Great Karst Grassland — Guide
item.description: Akiyoshidai is the largest karst plateau in Japan, a vast expanse of rolling green grassland in central Yamaguchi studded with countless jagged white limestone rocks that poke through the turf like grazing sheep. It sits directly above the Akiyoshido cave, the two forming a single geological wonder shaped by rain dissolving limestone over aeons. A scenic road crosses the plateau, walking trails wind among the rocks, and an observation deck takes in the whole sweep of it.

item.title: Aso Caldera Farm & Horse Riding — Guide
item.description: The wide, rolling grasslands of the Aso caldera — grazed by cattle and horses for centuries and kept open by traditional burning — are the perfect setting for farm experiences and horse riding. At ranches and farm parks around the caldera, visitors can ride horses across open pasture with the volcanic peaks as a backdrop, take pony rides, feed and meet cows, horses, sheep and other farm animals, and try hands-on activities like milking or butter-making.

item.title: Shikoku Karst: A Highland of Cattle and Sky — Guide
item.description: The Shikoku Karst is one of Japan’s three great karst plateaus, a striking highland running along the Ehime–Kochi border at around 1,400 metres. Here rolling green grassland stretches to the horizon, studded with weathered white limestone rocks and grazed by cattle in summer, under enormous open skies — a landscape utterly unlike the rest of mountainous Shikoku. A scenic skyline road runs along the plateau, passing viewpoints, a campground and windmills, with sweeping panoramas over range after range of Shikoku’s mountains.
